content: I'm happy to announce the following masterclass on formalisation in Lean, June 26-30 in Copenhagen: https://www.math.ku.dk/english/calendar/events/formalisation-of-mathematics/. The speakers are Kevin Buzzard and Adam Topaz, and it should be interesting to many people in this community. The plan is to present LTE in some detail, and the hope is that participants will learn the skills necessary to be able to contribute to such projects and work on their own formalisation projects. Registration will open in the spring.

Is the masterclass for PhD students, post-docs, or anyone?

Anyone! Note the prerequisites though:
"Participants are expected to be familiar with condensed mathematics (at least the first two Lectures in Scholze’s lecture notes: https://www.math.uni-bonn.de/people/scholze/Condensed.pdf), have some experience with formalisation of mathematics (not necessarily in Lean 4), and bring a computer with Lean 4 installed ( https://leanprover.github.io/lean4/doc/quickstart.html)."
Those prerequisites are pretty drastic, are you sure you'll get any participants?
I don't think they're drastic. If someone is keen on coming to the masterclass but doesn't fulfil all the prerequisites, they have almost four months to change that :)

Patrick Massot said:

Those prerequisites are pretty drastic, are you sure you'll get any participants?

You are right it may sound slightly intimidating given that we aim for an audience including students and non-mathlib contributors. It is however meant to say that we will be working with material covered in Scholze's notes (whose first chapters are quite accessible) from the get go, and that we also hope that participants are set up to start working with it in Lean 4 during the week of the masterclass as opposed starting from square one.

One of our main objectives with this masterclass is to bridge the gap for people that have toyed a bit or a lot with Lean to get onboard a bigger project and start contributing. I, as one of the organizers, fall into this category
